description: Dart reasoning, asynchronous work, widget identity, architecture, and production Flutter problems.

courses.title: Flutter & Dart Interviews
courses.description: Dart reasoning, asynchronous work, widget identity, architecture, and production Flutter problems.

chapters.title: 1 · Dart language reasoning
chapters.summary: Use null safety, equality, collections, and patterns deliberately.

lessons.title: Null safety and values
lessons.explanation: Reason about contracts at API boundaries.

exercises.prompt: An API nickname may be an empty but valid string. Which expression uses Guest only for null?
exercises.explanation: Null coalescing preserves an empty string and replaces only null.

exercises.prompt: A late non-null field is read before assignment. What happens?
options: The field is initialized from the type
exercises.explanation: late defers the initialization check to runtime; it does not create a value.

exercises.prompt: A final list is mutated through add. What happens?
options: A new list is assigned to items
The list contains a and b
exercises.explanation: final fixes the variable binding. It does not make the referenced List immutable.

exercises.prompt: An immutable compile-time list is required. Which declaration enforces no add at runtime?
exercises.explanation: A const list is immutable. final only prevents rebinding the variable.

exercises.prompt: Two distinct model instances with identical fields compare unequal by default. What must change for value equality?
options: Implement == and hashCode consistently or use a value model generator
Put both objects in a List
exercises.explanation: Dart objects use identity equality by default unless the class overrides it.

exercises.prompt: A mutable generic collection is passed through a broader type and then receives an incompatible value. What should the design avoid?
options: Unsound writes through runtime-checked covariant paths
exercises.explanation: Dart may insert runtime type checks for covariant generic assignments; clear ownership and type-safe APIs avoid surprises.

exercises.prompt: A sealed response model has success and failure cases. What is a good reason to use a switch expression?
options: The analyzer can help enforce coverage of the closed cases
exercises.explanation: Exhaustive patterns make missing state handling visible when the model evolves.

exercises.prompt: Fill the operator that uses a fallback only when the value is null.
exercises.explanation: Dart ?? checks null; an empty string remains unchanged.

exercises.prompt: A map update should retain prior keys and change one value. Which expression produces a new map?
exercises.explanation: The spread copies entries and the later key overrides b, leaving old unchanged.

exercises.prompt: You call where on an Iterable and mutate the source before iterating. What should be considered?
options: where is lazy, so later iteration can see the changed source
exercises.explanation: Iterable.where evaluates when consumed; call toList for a snapshot when needed.

exercises.prompt: A stream of sensor IDs needs per-sensor counts. Complete the one-pass aggregation.
exercises.hiddenTests: For [a,b,a], return {a:2,b:1}; for empty input return an empty map.

guided.explanation: A map stores one count per distinct ID. Default missing counts to zero before incrementing.

exercises.explanation: A map stores one count per distinct ID. Default missing counts to zero before incrementing.

exercises.prompt: A function returns both a parsed value and warning count without creating a class. Which Dart feature fits?
options: A Future with two generic parameters
A late field on a global object
A record such as (value: parsed, warnings: count)
exercises.explanation: Records carry a fixed group of typed values, including named fields.

exercises.prompt: A String extension adds isValidID. Does it override an existing String member of the same name?
options: No, instance members take precedence over extensions
exercises.explanation: Extensions are statically resolved helpers and cannot override instance members.

exercises.prompt: A widget list includes a warning tile only when hasError. Which collection syntax expresses this without a nullable child?
exercises.explanation: Collection if conditionally includes a real Widget; a nullable element would not satisfy List<Widget>.

exercises.prompt: firstWhere on an Iterable finds no match and has no orElse. What occurs?
exercises.explanation: Provide orElse or use a nullable search helper when absence is expected.

exercises.prompt: Fill the spread expression that copies entries before overriding status.
exercises.explanation: A map spread inserts prior entries; the later status key wins.

chapters.title: 2 · Async Dart
chapters.summary: Understand event ordering, streams, isolates, and cancellation.

lessons.title: Futures and scheduling
lessons.explanation: Separate asynchronous waits from CPU work.

exercises.prompt: What type does an async function returning 7 expose to its caller?
exercises.explanation: An async function wraps its result in a Future that callers await.

exercises.prompt: An awaited Future throws. Where can the caller handle the error?
options: Only in a global error handler
With a synchronous return after await
exercises.explanation: An async error propagates through await and can be caught in the surrounding async function.

exercises.prompt: A microtask and a zero-duration Timer are scheduled on the same isolate. Which normally runs first after current synchronous code?
exercises.explanation: Dart drains the microtask queue before taking the next event queue item. Avoid relying on complex timing beyond this rule.

exercises.prompt: Three independent requests must all succeed to build a screen. Which API starts and awaits them together?
options: Timer.run for each then return immediately
await each request before starting the next
exercises.explanation: Future.wait observes multiple independent Futures and returns their results when all complete.

exercises.prompt: Decoding a huge JSON payload causes visible frame stalls. What moves CPU work off the UI isolate?
options: Run parsing in another isolate, such as Isolate.run for suitable data
Wrap the same synchronous parser in Future.value
Call await before each loop iteration with no work split
exercises.explanation: An isolate gives CPU parsing another event loop; Future wrapping alone does not move synchronous work.

exercises.prompt: A screen disposes while an HTTP Future is pending. What is true about Dart Future itself?
options: Calling Future.cancel always stops the socket
A Timer converts it to a Stream
A Future does not provide general cancellation; cancel the underlying operation or ignore stale results
exercises.explanation: Cancellation depends on the underlying API. A mounted/generation guard prevents late UI updates.

exercises.prompt: A request timeout fires. Can the underlying operation always be assumed canceled?
options: No; timeout of the Future does not guarantee underlying work stopped
exercises.explanation: Use the client cancellation facility when available; a timed-out operation may still finish.

exercises.prompt: Fill the expression that catches an asynchronous fetch error in this function.
exercises.template: try { final rows = ____1 repository.fetchRows(); } catch (error) { report(error); }
exercises.explanation: await turns the Future failure into a throw at this call site.

lessons.title: Streams and ownership
lessons.explanation: Keep subscriptions and latest results under control.

exercises.prompt: A State object listens to a long-lived stream. What should happen in dispose?
exercises.explanation: Canceling releases the screen listener and prevents updates after its lifetime.

exercises.prompt: A single-subscription stream already has one listener. What happens when a second listener is attached?
options: The first listener is silently canceled
exercises.explanation: Single-subscription streams allow one listener; use a broadcast stream when multiple observers are intended.

exercises.prompt: A broadcast stream emits before a listener subscribes. What should a new listener expect by default?
exercises.explanation: Broadcast streams normally do not retain past events; state needs explicit replay or storage.

exercises.prompt: Search A starts, then B; A finishes last. Which guard keeps B visible?
options: Keep a single global loading Boolean
Wait a fixed 100 ms before A
Apply a result only when its request generation is current
Apply the last response to arrive
exercises.explanation: Generation checks reject stale responses independently of timing.

exercises.prompt: A stream subscription has no onError and the stream emits an error. What should be designed?
options: Put a try/catch only around listen construction
An explicit error handler or transformation at the owning boundary
Ignore errors because listen always retries
Convert all errors to empty success
exercises.explanation: Asynchronous stream errors need a handler or await-for error path, not just a synchronous try around listen.

exercises.prompt: A sensor emits faster than the UI can render. What is a sensible display policy?
options: Sample or coalesce readings for UI while retaining raw data only if required
Call setState for every reading without limit
Block the sensor callback on a frame
exercises.explanation: UI often needs the latest representative state rather than every high-frequency event.

exercises.prompt: A login event stream has rapid duplicate states. What should be checked before adding a custom distinct transform?
options: Whether each event has a random ID
Whether equality correctly expresses the state and whether losing identical events is acceptable
exercises.explanation: Deduplication is correct only when equal states are semantically interchangeable.

exercises.prompt: Fill the lifecycle action for a stream subscription owned by a State object.
exercises.explanation: Cancel the subscription when its owning State is disposed.

chapters.title: 3 · Widgets and lifecycle
chapters.summary: Use element identity, keys, and layout constraints correctly.

exercises.prompt: A parent rebuild creates a new Widget configuration of the same type and key. What usually happens to the existing Element?
options: It updates the existing Element with the new Widget
It always destroys the entire subtree
It skips all child updates automatically
exercises.explanation: Widgets are immutable descriptions; compatible type and key let the framework update the existing Element.

exercises.prompt: A network request placed directly in build fires repeatedly. Where should the work begin?
options: In an owned lifecycle action or an external state layer, with a stable dependency
exercises.explanation: build can run often and must remain side-effect free; start work at a deliberate lifecycle boundary.

exercises.prompt: An async callback calls setState after its State was disposed. What should be done?
options: Keep the old State in a static field
Cancel the work when possible and guard with mounted before updating
Call setState again until it succeeds
exercises.explanation: A disposed State cannot update UI. Ownership and a mounted check avoid late mutations.

exercises.prompt: Rows with local checkbox state reorder. Which key ties the state to the same record?
exercises.explanation: Stable domain IDs let the element tree preserve state by item identity across moves.

exercises.prompt: A list has hundreds of rows. Why should GlobalKey not be the default for each row?
options: It has wider identity and reparenting costs than local stable keys
It forces all rows to be const
exercises.explanation: ValueKey is usually enough for sibling identity; GlobalKey has more expensive global semantics.

exercises.prompt: A State method needs an inherited dependency during initialization. Which callback is designed for dependency changes?
exercises.explanation: didChangeDependencies runs after initState and when an inherited dependency changes.

exercises.prompt: Which layer performs layout and painting in Flutter?
exercises.explanation: Widgets configure, Elements manage instances, and RenderObjects handle layout/paint when relevant.

exercises.prompt: Fill the guard before updating UI after a Future resolves.
exercises.explanation: mounted is false after this State has been disposed.

lessons.title: Constraints and scrolling
lessons.explanation: Diagnose layout failures and large-list cost.

exercises.prompt: A ListView inside a Column throws an unbounded height error. What usually fixes the constraint?
options: Wrap the ListView in Expanded to give it bounded remaining height
Put a second ListView around it
Set every child width to infinity
exercises.explanation: A vertical scroll view needs a finite height constraint in this Column layout.

exercises.prompt: Expanded is placed directly inside a SingleChildScrollView column and fails. Why?
options: The scroll direction offers unbounded height, so there is no finite remaining space to expand into
exercises.explanation: Flex expansion requires bounded main-axis space; restructure the scrollable layout.

exercises.prompt: A feed has 20,000 rows. Which constructor avoids building all rows up front?
options: ListView.builder with stable keys where needed
exercises.explanation: builder creates visible items lazily, reducing initial work and memory pressure.

exercises.prompt: Setting shrinkWrap: true on a large nested list appears to solve constraints. What trade-off needs review?
options: It can require more layout work and weaken lazy scrolling benefits
It always makes the list faster
exercises.explanation: shrinkWrap measures content extent and can be costly; prefer a bounded list or sliver layout for large data.

exercises.prompt: A parent updates frequently. Where can const help in a static child subtree?
options: Canonicalize unchanged Widget configurations and reduce unnecessary reconstruction work
Guarantee no RenderObject ever paints again
Stop all inherited dependencies from updating
exercises.explanation: const is useful for truly static widget configurations, but it does not replace profiling or state isolation.

exercises.prompt: A Row child with long text overflows horizontally. Which widget can constrain it to remaining width?
options: Another Row with no width constraint
exercises.explanation: Expanded provides a finite width for text to wrap or ellipsize within the Row.

exercises.prompt: A small animated indicator causes a complex neighboring chart to repaint. What may isolate paint work?
options: A RepaintBoundary around a measured repaint region
exercises.explanation: RepaintBoundary can contain repaint propagation, but measure layer cost before applying broadly.

exercises.prompt: Fill the lazy scrolling constructor for a long result set.
exercises.template: final list = ListView.____1(itemCount: rows.length, itemBuilder: buildRow);
exercises.explanation: ListView.builder creates children as needed for scrolling.

chapters.title: 4 · State and architecture
chapters.summary: Choose ownership, immutable state, and testable boundaries.

lessons.title: State ownership
lessons.explanation: Match state mechanisms to scope and update frequency.

exercises.prompt: A small isolated toggle needs one observable value. Which built-in tool may be sufficient?
options: ValueNotifier<bool> with a listener or ValueListenableBuilder
A global mutable bool with no notification
A database migration for every tap
A new Isolate for the toggle
exercises.explanation: ValueNotifier is suitable for simple local observable state when ownership and disposal are clear.

exercises.prompt: A ChangeNotifier holds List<Item>. A caller mutates that list directly. Why might listeners miss the change?
options: Widgets poll the list every millisecond
notifyListeners is not called by arbitrary list mutation
exercises.explanation: Encapsulate mutation in the owner and notify after state changes, or expose immutable snapshots.

exercises.prompt: Two screens need the same cart state. Where should its provider live?
options: As a new provider on every build
At a shared ancestor whose lifetime covers both screens
exercises.explanation: The state owner must outlive the consumers that need a coherent cart.

exercises.prompt: An auto-disposed provider starts a request. What should happen when no listeners remain?
options: Write to a global variable without checks
Release or cancel owned work using the provider disposal hook where supported
Keep the request forever by default
Call setState in a dead widget
exercises.explanation: Provider lifetime should govern work ownership; disposal can stop a request or prevent stale delivery.

exercises.prompt: A BLoC receives AddItem twice quickly. Which design avoids a lost update?
options: Process events against the latest owned state with a defined concurrency policy
Read an old snapshot in two parallel handlers and overwrite with each result
Use a random delay before emit
exercises.explanation: Event ordering and transformer choice affect concurrent handlers; update from current state or serialize dependent operations.

exercises.prompt: Why publish a new immutable state object after a repository update?
options: It makes every API response valid
Consumers can observe a clear value transition without shared mutable aliases
exercises.explanation: Immutable snapshots clarify ownership and make equality and tests more predictable.

exercises.prompt: A screen model depends on network data. What allows a deterministic unit test?
options: Use a real server in every unit test
Read a global singleton with hidden state
Inject a repository interface and supply an in-memory fake
exercises.explanation: A replaceable dependency isolates business decisions from the network.

exercises.prompt: Fill the notification after a ChangeNotifier updates its private state.
exercises.explanation: ChangeNotifier must notify listeners after its owned state changes.

lessons.title: Consistency and tests
lessons.explanation: Keep data authoritative across view changes and failures.

exercises.prompt: A screen observes database rows while a refresh fetches newer rows. Which layer should apply the response?
options: A static List with no persistence
Repository writes validated rows to local storage, which emits to UI
Each widget overwrites its own local copy
Network callback directly mutates child State objects
exercises.explanation: One local source of truth keeps offline and refreshed views consistent.

exercises.prompt: Loading, loaded, and failed are mutually exclusive. What is a robust Dart model?
options: A sealed state family with data on the relevant cases
Three unrelated bools and nullable data
One status string with dynamic payload
exercises.explanation: A closed state model prevents contradictory combinations and makes exhaustive UI decisions possible.

exercises.prompt: A liked item is shown immediately before server confirmation. What must happen if the server rejects it?
options: Delete every item in the feed
Retry with a new action ID indefinitely
Rollback or reconcile the optimistic change and tell the user
exercises.explanation: Optimistic updates need a failure path tied to the same operation.

exercises.prompt: Two screens show the same account balance. What reduces drift?
options: Use separate timers to refresh randomly
Both observe one repository-owned state source
Each cache a mutable copy indefinitely
exercises.explanation: Shared authoritative state lets both screens reflect the same committed value.

exercises.prompt: A widget test taps Retry after a request error. What should it assert?
options: The retry callback occurs and the visible state changes appropriately
Only that the source contains the word Retry
exercises.explanation: Behavioral assertions survive refactors while verifying the learner-facing flow.

exercises.prompt: A debounce test uses real waiting and is flaky. How should it be improved?
options: Inject or control the scheduler/clock and advance fake time
Run it only on fast machines
exercises.explanation: Controllable time makes event ordering reproducible and tests fast.

exercises.prompt: A new screen subscribes after a price update. It must show the current price immediately. What should the source provide?
options: A new price guessed from UI text
A current state value or queryable repository snapshot
exercises.explanation: State has a current value; one-off event streams can miss updates while a screen is absent.

exercises.prompt: Fill the state case used to render an explicit recoverable failure.
exercises.template: switch (state) { case Loading(): return spinner; case Loaded(:final rows): return list(rows); case ____1: return retry(error); }
exercises.explanation: An explicit failed variant carries the error needed for a retry UI.

chapters.title: 5 · Production Flutter scenarios
chapters.summary: Design reliable networking, navigation, platform integration, and performance.

lessons.title: Platform and performance
lessons.explanation: Protect smooth frames and native boundaries.

exercises.prompt: A Dart screen needs a device-only API. What should cross a platform channel?
options: Small serializable requests and results with explicit errors
exercises.explanation: Platform channels exchange supported values; keep the native boundary narrow and error-aware.

exercises.prompt: A long feed with many large images uses excessive memory. What is a reasonable first diagnosis?
options: Duplicate every image in a global list
Load original full-resolution files for thumbnails
Inspect decode dimensions, cache size, and offscreen image lifetime
exercises.explanation: Decoded images can cost far more memory than compressed files; size and lifetime matter.

exercises.prompt: An edit screen returns a saved item to its caller. Which navigation flow is appropriate?
options: Await the pushed route result and refresh by stable item ID
exercises.explanation: A route result communicates a completed action, while the repository remains authoritative for durable data.

exercises.prompt: A notification deep link opens a detail page before its data is cached. What should the destination do?
options: Open the last viewed item instead
Parse a stable ID, show loading, fetch or read locally, then handle missing data
Require a live object pointer in the URL
exercises.explanation: Deep links need restorable identifiers and explicit loading and not-found states.

exercises.prompt: A user saves a draft offline. Where should the save be committed before showing success?
options: Durable local storage with an explicit pending-sync state
Only a network request that cannot run
exercises.explanation: Local durability lets a draft survive process death; pending sync communicates remote status.

exercises.prompt: A POST may have committed before timing out. What enables a safe retry?
options: A fresh random key for every attempt
A stable idempotency key accepted by the server
exercises.explanation: The same operation ID lets the server deduplicate repeated delivery.

exercises.prompt: An animation janks only while a large synchronous transformation runs. What should you profile first?
options: The number of routes in pubspec
UI isolate frame time and the transformation cost
exercises.explanation: CPU work on the UI isolate competes with frame scheduling; profile before moving it.

exercises.prompt: Fill the async channel call that returns a native battery value.
exercises.explanation: invokeMethod sends a named method request over a MethodChannel.

lessons.title: Offline queue and recovery
lessons.explanation: Make uncertain outcomes and sync conflict explicit.

exercises.prompt: A server record changed after an offline local edit. What must sync decide?
options: Pick whichever value has a longer string
A documented conflict rule using revisions or domain merge semantics
Always discard the local edit silently
exercises.explanation: Arrival order alone cannot express user intent; versions reveal concurrent changes.

exercises.prompt: A charge request times out. Which state is honest before reconciliation?
exercises.explanation: A timeout does not prove whether the server committed the charge.

exercises.prompt: Two offline edits to the same record are queued. What must the uploader preserve or reconcile?
options: Only the last network arrival time
Their causal order or a defined versioned merge rule
exercises.explanation: Out-of-order delivery can undo later edits unless operations or versions encode the dependency.

exercises.prompt: A native plugin throws during checkout. What should a diagnostic report include?
options: A correlation ID and sanitized error category
Full payment tokens and card details
exercises.explanation: Sanitized context supports debugging without exposing sensitive values.

exercises.prompt: The app resumes after hours offline. What should trigger a safe refresh?
options: A lifecycle-aware refresh policy that keeps cached data visible
Run a request in every widget build
exercises.explanation: Resume can prompt a refresh, but existing offline data remains usable while it runs.

exercises.prompt: An isolate returns a parsed snapshot after the active course changed. What prevents stale application?
options: Check request/course generation before committing the result
Always write the result to the current course
exercises.explanation: Moving work off the UI isolate does not remove races between old and new requests.

exercises.prompt: Fill the stable identifier passed across retries of one command.
exercises.explanation: One command must retain the same ID for deduplication after timeouts.

exercises.prompt: Queue an offline edit safely
exercises.story: A profile edit is saved without network. The worker can restart and the HTTP response may be lost. Complete the staged queue.

parts.hiddenTests: A saved edit yields one durable command with its original operation ID before scheduling.

guided.explanation: Retain the edit operation ID, insert the command, then schedule delivery.

parts.expected: Retain the edit operation ID, insert the command, then schedule delivery.

parts.prompt: Settle confirmed and uncertain outcomes differently.
parts.hiddenTests: Confirmed delivery marks one command complete; uncertain delivery keeps it pending for a same-key retry.

guided.explanation: Send with the stable key, complete only confirmed commands, and retry uncertain outcomes.

parts.expected: Send with the stable key, complete only confirmed commands, and retry uncertain outcomes.
